newsitem.title: USA: Army's top enlisted man faces new sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Army's top enlisted man faces new sex charges.

text.p: The Army's highest-ranking enlisted soldier will face new charges of sexual misconduct involving a fifth alleged victim, the Army said Friday.

Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney, who already faces 18 counts involving four service women, now has been charged with assault on an officer and solicitation of adultery with her, the Army said in a news release.

"Additional criminal charges under the Uniform Code of Military Justice were preferred against Sergeant Major of the Army, Gene C. McKinney, today," the Army said. "Both specifications involve the same commissioned officer and allegedly occurred between March and August 1994."

The accusations were the first against McKinney involving an officer. The other allegations, including adultery and indecent assault, involve enlisted women, three from the Army and one from the Navy.

The Army is conducting a preliminary hearing against McKinney to determine whether he should be court-martialed on the other charges, which he has denied. If convicted on all those counts, he could face 45 years in prison.

Assault on a commissioned officer, one of the new charges, carries a maximum penalty of 10 years confinement, dishonourable discharge, total forfeiture of all pay and allowances, and reduction to the lowest enlisted grade.
